:::{#def-two-part-description-length}
#### Two-part description length

Let $\vx$ be data,
and let $p_1, \ldots, p_m$ be models,
each of which gives $\vx$ a [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $p_j(\vx)$.
Let a [prefix code](huffman-codes.qmd#def-prefix-code) on the models give each model $p_j$ a codeword of $\codelenf{p_j}$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit).

The **two-part description length** of $\vx$ under a model $p_j$ is

$$\codelenf{p_j} + \surprisalunderf{p_j}{\vx}.$$

The first part is the length of the codeword that names the model.
The second part is the [surprisal](entropy.qmd#def-surprisal) $\log_2 \frac{1}{p_j(\vx)}$ of $\vx$ under the model,
which is the length in bits of a [code](source-coding.qmd#def-code) for $\vx$ built from the model.

:::
